findings.issue_text: The addGuests handler authorizes any booking attendee (not just the organizer) to add guests, so any user who books a meeting with a victim can add arbitrary attendees and trigger emails that disclose the meeting's video-call credentials (meetingUrl/meetingPassword) to attacker-chosen addresses

The guests array schema (z.array(z.string().email())) has no .max() limit and the handler has no rate limiting, allowing unbounded mass-email dispatch and unbounded createMany of Attendee rows per request
The isTeamAdminOrOwner check uses && instead of ||, requiring the caller to be both admin AND owner, which incorrectly denies team admins who are not owners from managing guests on team bookings

The blacklisted email comparison is case-sensitive: the denylist entries are lowercased but the submitted guest email retains its original casing, allowing BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS to be bypassed (e.g. Banned@Example.com); the same case-sensitivity in guest === attendee.email allows duplicate attendees to be re-added under different casing

The calendar update builds the EventManager with the caller's (ctx.user) OAuth credentials instead of the booking organizer's credentials (which were already loaded), causing wrong-account credential use and leaving committed attendee rows without calendar sync on failure since the DB write is not transactional with this step

There is no booking.status check, so guests can be added to CANCELLED/REJECTED bookings, and the ICS attachment hardcodes status: 'CONFIRMED', causing cancelled events to be resurrected on attendees' calendars via fresh confirmed invites

Email uniqueness is only enforced client-side: the server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema drops the uniqueness refine that AddGuestsDialog has, so a direct tRPC call with duplicate emails in the array passes validation and createMany inserts duplicate Attendee rows

addGuests.handler.ts: The Attendee DB rows are committed via prisma.booking.update/createMany (lines 92-106) before the external calendar write (eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees, line ~160) with no transaction, compensation, or rollback — if the calendar API call throws, guests are persisted in the DB but never propagated to the calendar or emailed, causing permanent DB↔calendar divergence.

addGuests.handler.ts: The retry path after a failed calendar write is permanently blocked — resubmitting the same emails causes the attendee-dedup filter (lines 74-78) to empty uniqueGuests and the guard (lines 80-81) to throw BAD_REQUEST emails_must_be_unique_valid, and there is no remove-guest endpoint to undo and redo, so the user cannot re-trigger calendar propagation without manual DB surgery.

addGuests.schema.ts: The server input schema uses z.array(z.string().email()) without the duplicate-email .refine validation the client (AddGuestsDialog.tsx) enforces, and the handler's uniqueGuests filter does not dedupe emails within the submitted list — API clients can submit duplicates, persisting duplicate Attendee rows (person double-counted against seat capacity, duplicate emails, listed twice on the calendar) or surfacing an unhandled Prisma P2002 as a raw 500.

addGuests.handler.ts: The read of booking.attendees (lines 26-42) and the attendee write (lines 92-106) are not in a transaction, so two concurrent addGuests requests can both pass the uniqueness filter and create duplicate Attendee rows (TOCTOU race).

addGuests.handler.ts (lines 70-78): Blacklist entries from BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS are lowercased but guest emails are compared as-typed, so a case variant like Guest@Example.com bypasses a blacklisted guest@example.com and creates a permanent Attendee row (plus emails sent and calendar updated) for an address the deployment explicitly banned.

addGuests.handler.ts: The attendee dedup uses an exact case-sensitive comparison (guest === attendee.email), so a case-variant of an existing attendee's stored email defeats the dedup and writes a second persistent record for the same person that no later exact-match code path will recognize as the same human.

addGuests.handler.ts (lines 153-160): The EventManager used to update the organizer's calendar event is constructed with the caller's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the organizer's — the organizer's credentials are fetched but never used.

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The addGuests handler authorizes any booking attendee (not just the organizer) to add guests, so any user who books a meeting with a victim can add arbitrary attendees and trigger emails that disclose the meeting's video-call credentials (meetingUrl/meetingPassword) to attacker-chosen addresses

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, authorization explicitly allows any booking attendee: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and access is granted unless `!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee`. That means a non-organizer attendee can call `addGuests` and add arbitrary `guests` emails via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`. The handler then builds a `CalendarEvent` `evt` and, if a `_video` reference exists, attaches `evt.videoCallData` including `meetingUrl`/`meetingPassword`. It then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which sends emails to attendees (including newly added addresses) based on this `calendarEvent`, so the added recipients can receive event details that may include video-call credentials. This is directly supported by the diff and constitutes a real security concern if attendees are not intended to be able to invite arbitrary additional guests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The guests array schema (z.array(z.string().email())) has no .max() limit and the handler has no rate limiting, allowing unbounded mass-email dispatch and unbounded createMany of Attendee rows per request

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the new TRPC mutation `viewer.bookings.addGuests` uses `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` with `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` and no `.max()` (or similar) bound. In `addGuestsHandler`, the handler builds `uniqueGuests` from the provided `guests` and then performs `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany({ data: guestsFullDetails }))`, where `guestsFullDetails` scales with the size of the request. It also calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which constructs `emailsToSend` including organizer/team-member emails plus one per attendee, so the email fan-out can grow with the number of added guests. There is no per-request cap or rate limiting shown in the diff, so a single authenticated caller with permission could submit a very large array and trigger large DB writes and mass email dispatch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The isTeamAdminOrOwner check uses && instead of ||, requiring the caller to be both admin AND owner, which incorrectly denies team admins who are not owners from managing guests on team bookings
matched_golden_ids: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments identify the same bug: the permission check for admin/owner uses logical AND (&&) instead of OR (||), incorrectly requiring a user to be both admin and owner rather than either one.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The blacklisted email comparison is case-sensitive: the denylist entries are lowercased but the submitted guest email retains its original casing, allowing BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS to be bypassed (e.g. Banned@Example.com); the same case-sensitivity in guest === attendee.email allows duplicate attendees to be re-added under different casing

The calendar update builds the EventManager with the caller's (ctx.user) OAuth credentials instead of the booking organizer's credentials (which were already loaded), causing wrong-account credential use and leaving committed attendee rows without calendar sync on failure since the DB write is not transactional with this step

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the calendar sync is performed via `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` after the DB update. The EventManager is constructed with `...user` where `user` is `ctx.user` (the caller) and credentials from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, even though the booking includes `user.credentials` and the organizer is derived from `booking.userId`. If a team admin/attendee triggers this mutation, the calendar update will attempt to use the caller’s OAuth credentials rather than the booking organizer’s, which is a concrete wrong-account credential usage risk. Additionally, `prisma.booking.update(... createMany attendees ...)` commits before the calendar update and is not wrapped in a transaction with the external calendar update; if `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the new attendee rows remain persisted without calendar sync.

adjudication_records.issue_text: There is no booking.status check, so guests can be added to CANCELLED/REJECTED bookings, and the ICS attachment hardcodes status: 'CONFIRMED', causing cancelled events to be resurrected on attendees' calendars via fresh confirmed invites

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` fetches the booking by `id` and authorizes by role, but it never checks any booking lifecycle state (e.g., cancelled/rejected) before mutating attendees and sending updates. Separately, the newly added email templates explicitly generate ICS with `status: "CONFIRMED"` (`packages/emails/templates/attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`) and `method: "REQUEST"`. If this endpoint is used on a cancelled/rejected booking, it would still send a fresh CONFIRMED invite/update, which can reasonably re-add/reconfirm the event in recipients’ calendars.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email uniqueness is only enforced client-side: the server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema drops the uniqueness refine that AddGuestsDialog has, so a direct tRPC call with duplicate emails in the array passes validation and createMany inserts duplicate Attendee rows
matched_golden_ids: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying bug: duplicate emails within the submitted input array are not deduplicated/validated on the server, so createMany can insert duplicate Attendee rows when a client (e.g., via direct tRPC call) submits repeated emails. The candidate frames it as missing server-side uniqueness validation, which matches the golden concern about uniqueGuests not deduping input duplicates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts: The Attendee DB rows are committed via prisma.booking.update/createMany (lines 92-106) before the external calendar write (eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees, line ~160) with no transaction, compensation, or rollback — if the calendar API call throws, guests are persisted in the DB but never propagated to the calendar or emailed, causing permanent DB↔calendar divergence.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the handler first persists new attendees via prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}}) and only afterwards calls the external side-effect eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking). There is no surrounding DB transaction that also encompasses the calendar update, and there is no try/catch/compensation around updateCalendarAttendees (only sendAddGuestsEmails is in a try/catch). Therefore, if updateCalendarAttendees throws (e.g., calendar API failure), the DB change has already been committed while the calendar update and subsequent email sending will not happen, leaving a persistent DB↔calendar mismatch for that booking.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts: The retry path after a failed calendar write is permanently blocked — resubmitting the same emails causes the attendee-dedup filter (lines 74-78) to empty uniqueGuests and the guard (lines 80-81) to throw BAD_REQUEST emails_must_be_unique_valid, and there is no remove-guest endpoint to undo and redo, so the user cannot re-trigger calendar propagation without manual DB surgery.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In addGuests.handler.ts the DB is updated first (prisma.booking.update with createMany for guestsFullDetails) and only afterwards it calls eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking) with no try/catch or rollback. If updateCalendarAttendees throws (calendar write failure), the handler will fail after having already persisted the new attendees. On a retry with the same emails, the dedup filter (`!booking.attendees.some(...)`) will filter them all out because they now exist in booking.attendees, making uniqueGuests empty and triggering the BAD_REQUEST guard (`if (uniqueGuests.length === 0) throw ...`). This creates a real “can’t retry the same add” failure mode after a partial failure. The finding’s extra claim about there being no remove-guest endpoint isn’t verifiable from the diff, but the blocked-retry-after-partial-failure behavior is verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.schema.ts: The server input schema uses z.array(z.string().email()) without the duplicate-email .refine validation the client (AddGuestsDialog.tsx) enforces, and the handler's uniqueGuests filter does not dedupe emails within the submitted list — API clients can submit duplicates, persisting duplicate Attendee rows (person double-counted against seat capacity, duplicate emails, listed twice on the calendar) or surfacing an unhandled Prisma P2002 as a raw 500.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows client-side validation in AddGuestsDialog via `z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)` to enforce uniqueness, but the server-side `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` in `addGuests.schema.ts` is only `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness check. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out emails already in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted emails, but it does not dedupe duplicates within the submitted `guests` array itself (e.g., `['a@x.com','a@x.com']` would pass through both if not already an attendee/blacklisted). Those duplicates are then passed to `attendees.createMany.data`, so the API can accept duplicate inputs and attempt to create duplicate attendee rows; whether that results in duplicated rows or a DB constraint error depends on schema not shown, but the lack of server-side uniqueness enforcement and deduping is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts: The read of booking.attendees (lines 26-42) and the attendee write (lines 92-106) are not in a transaction, so two concurrent addGuests requests can both pass the uniqueness filter and create duplicate Attendee rows (TOCTOU race).

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the handler first reads the current attendees via prisma.booking.findFirst({ include: { attendees: true, ... } }) and computes uniqueGuests by filtering against booking.attendees, then later performs a separate prisma.booking.update(...) with attendees.createMany({ data: guestsFullDetails }). Because these are separate operations with no transaction/locking, two concurrent addGuests requests for the same booking can both compute the same uniqueGuests from the same pre-update attendee snapshot and then both attempt to insert. Unless there is an (unshown) database-level unique constraint or createMany option (e.g., skipDuplicates) to prevent it, this is a classic TOCTOU race that can result in duplicate attendee rows or a nondeterministic failure on one request.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same case-sensitivity bug: the blacklist is lowercased but the input guest email is compared without lowercasing, allowing uppercase variants to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts: The attendee dedup uses an exact case-sensitive comparison (guest === attendee.email), so a case-variant of an existing attendee's stored email defeats the dedup and writes a second persistent record for the same person that no later exact-match code path will recognize as the same human.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the filter for existing attendees uses a case-sensitive comparison: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`. Since the input schema (`z.string().email()`) does not normalize casing, a user can submit a case-variant of an existing attendee email (e.g., `Test@ex.com` vs `test@ex.com`) and it will not be considered a duplicate, resulting in a second attendee record being created for the same email address in different casing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts (lines 153-160): The EventManager used to update the organizer's calendar event is constructed with the caller's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the organizer's — the organizer's credentials are fetched but never used.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler builds `eventManager` with `...user` where `user` is `ctx.user` (the caller) and sets `credentials` from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. The booking’s organizer is separately fetched into `organizer`, but those details are only used to populate `evt.organizer` and defaults for new guests; no organizer credentials are fetched/used. Since permission allows non-organizers (team admin/owner or an attendee) to call this mutation, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` may attempt to update the calendar event using the caller’s credentials rather than the organizer’s, which is a concrete correctness issue visible in the diff.
